source_text: Patiuntur hanc omnes ignominiam, qui indicunt veritati bellum. Nos ergo quod egimus colligamus. Quaeritur unde illa prima voluntas mala in homine fuerit exorta. Respondemus: A motu animi, cogente nullo. Obicitur: Si in opere Dei apparuit? Assentimur verum esse. Rogatur quomodo id non abnuamus, qui negamus naturale peccatum. Respondemus: Quia in opere Dei a possibili existit peccatum istud, non a necessario. Naturalia ergo necessaria sunt, possibilia autem voluntaria.
pass_a_gloss: All suffer this ignominy who declare war on truth. Let us therefore gather what we have done. It is asked from where that first evil will arose in the human. We reply: From a motion of the mind, no one compelling. It is objected: If it appeared in a work of God? We assent that it is true. It is asked how we do not deny that, we who deny a natural sin. We reply: Because in a work of God this sin exists from the possible, not from the necessary. Natural things therefore are necessary, but possible things voluntary.

pass_b_english: All who declare war on truth suffer this disgrace. Let us gather our result. The question is where that first evil will arose in a human being. We answer: from a movement of the mind under no compulsion. The objection asks whether it appeared in God’s work. We agree that this is true. We are asked how we do not deny that, although we deny natural sin. We answer: because this sin exists in God’s work from possibility, not necessity. Natural things, then, are necessary; possible things are voluntary.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
